look_here_first: Texas groundplum variety with thick green fleshy pods near the ground. The important look-alike is A. plattensis: compare ovary/pod HAIRS (groundplum generally glabrous versus hairy plattensis) and groove along each pod SUTURE, not just the pod's size.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; current Kew accepts var. berlandieri as a Texas-native variety.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae/Astragalus: alternate pinnate leaves, papilionoid pea flowers, and legumes; fruit shape, inflation, hairiness, and curvature are especially useful for species ID.
best_field_traits: alternate pinnate leaves with pea-type flowers
plum-like thick fleshy green pods, borne low
ovary and mature pod generally glabrous in groundplum comparison
similar A. plattensis has consistently hairy developing ovary/pod and conspicuously grooved mature fruit
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Not the only thick-podded genus member: A. plattensis also has green fleshy groundplum-like fruit and can be sympatric in south-central Texas. An ovary hair macro, 1 mm scale and mature suture-groove photo are necessary. Var. berlandieri is a distinct accepted taxon: photos of var. crassicarpus must not be labeled as this Texas variety.
